paper.title: Online combinatorial optimization with stochastic decision sets and adversarial losses

settings.name_in_paper: online combinatorial optimization with stochastic action availability, full information
unmapped: Available decision set S_t subset of S subseteq {0,1}^d is drawn i.i.d. from a fixed unknown distribution P each round, independently of history
Regret measured against the best fixed policy (choice function) mapping decision sets to actions
settings.definition_quote: the learner has to choose an action $\bV_t$ from a subset $\Sw_t$ of a known decision set $\Sw\subseteq\ev{0,1}^d$ with $\onenorm{\bv}\le m$ ... We assume that the environment selects $\Sw_t$ according to some fixed (but unknown) distribution $\P$ ... in the \emph{full information} setting, the learner observes $\bloss_{t}$

Decision sets drawn i.i.d. from unknown P
Regret against best fixed policy mapping decision sets to actions

settings.name_in_paper: sleeping experts with restricted feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Restricted feedback (losses of awake experts observed)
d experts, availability distribution picks one of d/2 pairs uniformly
settings.definition_quote: Consider a sleeping experts problem with $d$ experts ... Let $\P$ be such that it assigns a probability of $1/N$ to each pair $(2i-1,2i)$ of experts, that is, only two experts are awake at each time.

symbols.L_T_star: max{ min_pi E[sum_t pi(S_t)^T l_t], 4(log d + 1) }: expected loss of best policy, floored

source.label: thm:fullinfo
source.quote: Define $L_T^* = \max\ev{\min_\pi \EE{\sum_{t=1}^T \pi(\Sw_t)\transpose \bloss_t}, 4(\log d + 1)}$. Setting $\eta = \sqrt{(\log d + 1)/L_T^*}$, the regret of FPL in the full information scheme satisfies $R_T \le 2 m\sqrt{2 L_T^* (\log d + 1)}$.

results.notes: Regret is max_pi of sum of expectations (adversarial pseudo-regret against best policy). Proof uses 1-m*eta >= 1/2, which requires suitably large L_T^* relative to m; stated as 'by assumption of the theorem'. Learner needs L_T^* for tuning.

symbols.sum_Q: sum_{t=1}^T Q_t with Q_t = sum_i E[V_{t,i} | i in D_t]

source.label: thm:restricted
source.quote: Define $Q_t = \sum_{i=1}^d \EEcc{V_{t,i}}{i\in \D_t}$. The total expected regret of \SleepingCat against the best fixed policy is upper bounded as $R_T \le \frac{m(\log d + 1)}{\eta} + 2\eta m\sum_{t=1}^T Q_t.$

results.notes: Generic bound with free learning rate.

source.label: cor:rest_1
source.quote: Setting $\eta=\sqrt{(\log d + 1)/(2dT)}$, the regret of \SleepingCat against the best fixed policy is bounded as $R_T \le 2m\sqrt{2dT(\log d + 1)}$.

symbols.beta_a: lower bound on availability probabilities a_i = P[i in D_t] for all components

conditions: a_i >= beta for all components i

source.label: cor:rest_2
source.quote: Assuming $a_i\ge \beta$ for all $i$, we have $Q_t \le 1/\beta$, and setting $\eta=\sqrt{\beta(\log d + 1)/(2T)}$ guarantees that the regret of \SleepingCat against the best fixed policy is bounded as $R_T \le 2m\sqrt{\frac{2T(\log d + 1)}{\beta}}$.

results.notes: Tuning uses beta, which is not in learner_knows vocabulary.

symbols.M_gr: number of geometric resampling perturbations M
symbols.sum_Q: sum_{t=1}^T Q_t with Q_t = sum_i E[V_{t,i} | i in D_t]

source.label: thm:semibandit
source.quote: Define $Q_t = \sum_{i=1}^d \EEcc{V_{t,i}}{i\in D_t}$. The total expected regret of \SleepingCatBandit against the best fixed policy is bounded as $R_T \le \frac{m(\log d + 1)}{\eta} + 2\eta Mm\sum_{t=1}^T Q_t + \frac{dT}{eM}.$

Setting $\eta=\pa{\frac{\sqrt{m}(\log d + 1)}{2dT}}^{2/3}$ and $M = \frac {1}{\sqrt e} \cdot \pa{\frac{dT}{\sqrt{2} m (\log d + 1)}}^{1/3}$ guarantees that the regret of \SleepingCatBandit against the best fixed policy is bounded as $R_T \le (2mdT)^{2/3}\cdot (\log d+1)^{1/3}$.

results.notes: For K-armed sleeping bandit (S=[K]) gives (2KT)^{2/3}(log K+1)^{1/3}. Paper remarks d^{2/3} can be replaced by (d/beta)^{1/3} if a_i >= beta (not formally stated).

conditions: availability distribution uniform over d/2 disjoint pairs of experts

source.label: app:lowerbound
source.quote: showing that there exist sleeping experts problems for any even $d$ where the guarantees of Corollary~\ref{cor:rest_1} cannot be improved asymptotically.

results.notes: Informal appendix argument, not a numbered theorem. Asymptotic statement lim R_T/sqrt(TN) >= c for constant c > 0, with N = d/2.
